title: Task-focused surface map and routing heuristics (working notes)
body:
Purpose
This is a working, task-first exploration of console surface mapping and route heuristics to guide the sidebar redesign. Goal: reduce time-to-task for common flows (deploy, metrics, debugging), make deep links reliable for integrations, and enable progressive rollouts (canary, flag-driven UX).

Context & constraints
- Console growth: feature surface has grown horizontally — users lose contextual anchors when switching between routes.
- Performance budget: cold nav transition target < 200ms for shell load; tokenized panels should lazy-load.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first focus, ARIA landmarks, and clear focus management on navigation.
- Multiple deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private) must be discoverable without crowding primary task flow.

Guiding principles- Task-first: prioritize what users want to accomplish (create endpoint, inspect logs, rollouts) not internal feature taxonomy.
- Minimal visible chrome: surface tools when they’re relevant to the selected task.
- Deep-link stability: stable canonical URLs for integrations and saved links.
- Predictable fallbacks: deterministic behavior when route params are missing or broken.
- Observability-first: telemetry hooks on nav events, route latencies, and user abandon events.

Proposed top-level surface map (example)- Home / Overview: quick health cards, recent activity, shortcuts to active tasks.
- Endpoints: list + detail + quick actions (deploy, rollback, scale).
- Models: catalog, model versions, quantization profiles, test prompts.
- Jobs & Batches: training/eval jobs, batch embeddings.
- Observability: traces, token-cost breakdown, latency histograms.
- Rollouts: canary/configs/A-B experiments.
- Settings: org-level config, billing, teams, access.
Rationale: group by end-to-end job (e.g., deploy flow spans Models -> Endpoints -> Rollouts -> Observability). Keep Settings tucked away but reachable.

Sidebar modes (3 modes)
1) Compact (default for power users): single-column icons + hover/peek, persistent global search.
2) Task-focused (guided): expanded with task flows and shortcuts (used when user chooses "Focus" or onboards). Shows contextual quick actions and the task breadcrumb.
3) Admin (expanded): full text labels, org-level actions, audit logs and admin routes visible.

Behavioral rules for sidebar- Collapse/expand: persist preference per user (cookie + server-side preference).
- Contextual expansion: when deep-link hits a child route, ensure parent highlighted and if compact, auto-peek for 3s to show context.
- Shortcut keys: `G` to open quick-nav, `T` to toggle task-focus.
- Mobile: bottom sheet nav (fewer top-level items; most common 4 actions).

Routing heuristics and contracts- Canonical route pattern: /:org/:area/:resourceType/:resourceId(/:action) — e.g., /acme/endpoints/ep-123/metrics- Route robustness: if :resourceId missing or invalid, surface an inline recovery UI (search/autocomplete) instead of 404.
- Backwards-compatibility: old permalink formats must redirect server-side to new canonical routes (preserve slug mapping table).
- Query params: use querystring for ephemeral UI state only (filters, time-range). Persistent selection -> path segment.
- Route splitting for SSR vs client: shell is SSR for first meaningful paint; panel content lazy-loads via client routes.

Deep linking & integrations- Provide stable deep-link surface for partners (e.g., third-party alert links to an endpoint's trace).
- Add `linkToken` param for time-bound preview links for Private deployments (security).

State persistence & session model- Session vs. persistent: last-opened-panel per area stored persistently; ephemeral UI toggles in session storage.
- Cross-tab sync: use BroadcastChannel + server heartbeat to avoid conflicting write actions (e.g., two tabs editing rollout).

Microcopy & affordances- Breadcrumb treatment: show progressive breadcrumb for tasks, not raw resource ids. Example: "Models > llama-2-70b > quantization > Q4_8"
- Inline context tips for new users in Task-focused mode.

Wireframe notes (sketch-level, non-exhaustive)- Desktop task-focused: left 72px icon rail (compact) toggles to 260px panel with task shortcuts. Center column: workspace. Right column: contextual inspector (logs, traces).
- Mobile: bottom rounded nav with primary actions (Overview, Endpoints, Models, Search). Secondary actions in a 2-step menu.

Failure & fallback strategies- Nav shell failure: show stripped-down emergency shell with core shortcuts (Overview, Status page, Contact support).
- Missing data: render lightweight fallback cards with CTA "Retry / Search / Open in safe mode".

Telemetry & rollout plan- Measure: time-to-first-action (TTFA), nav abandonment, deep-link click success rate, route-resolution error rate.
- Flags: backend flag for new route resolver (safe default: old resolver until parity).
- Canary cohort: 5% orgs with high activity, monitor TTFA and error budget.

Engineering constraints & perf notes- Keep nav prominence decisions decoupled from feature gating; nav layout changes are a product-level flag, not numerous feature flags.
- Avoid shipping large bundles: use dynamic imports for infrequently used admin panels.

Open questions (to resolve in grooming)
- How do we represent multi-tenant orgs with nested projects in the nav? Flatten or two-level?(Action: design spike, Diego).
- Should quick actions be configurable per org or fixed? (Security/permissions implications).
- Exact semantics of querystring vs path for timeline filters (affects linkability).

Next steps- Prototype the Task-focused panel in Figma and run a 3-user unmoderated test. (Aisha).
- Wire up route resolver to return structured route metadata for telemetry (Noah).
- Draft a rollout checklist with SRE for backward redirects and slug mapping (Eleanor).

Notes to self / TODOs- Add keyboard nav cheat-sheet to new user onboarding.
- Build a small script to scan existing links in docs and report 404/redirect risk.

Decision log (placeholder)- 2025-01-24: Agreed to keep Settings out of primary top-level nav, but add quick access from profile menu (decision by product sync).

Raw sketches & callouts- See attached Figma link for three low-fidelity flows: "Endpoint deploy happy path", "Investigate spike -> trace -> costs", "Admin audit -> team access change".

This is intentionally rough — trying to capture trade-offs and guardrails we can use for grooming. Please add comments inline in Figma or paste short notes here.

-- Mariana
